claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and crystalline.
The compared nanoparticles have controlled, uniform compositions but different diameters.
A controlled temperature ramp can compare melting behavior in approximately 5 nm and 10 nm FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Surface effects are pronounced in nanoparticles roughly below 10 nm.
The extent of surface disorder and the fraction of atoms at the surface mediate premelting.
Smaller nanoparticles have a larger proportion of surface atoms.
The larger surface-atom proportion in smaller particles enhances surface-energy effects.
Enhanced surface-energy effects lower the local energy barrier for atomic mobility.
A liquid-like surface layer forms before the particle core melts.
The liquid-like surface layer promotes subsequent melting into the particle core.
Smaller FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will begin surface premelting at lower temperatures than larger particles or bulk material.
Smaller nanoparticles will exhibit a more gradual and heterogeneous melting progression than larger particles or bulk material.
Bulk or very large FeNiCrCoCu samples melt at higher temperatures than small nanoparticles.
Bulk or very large FeNiCrCoCu samples melt relatively homogeneously without a pronounced premelting surface layer.
Interfacial segregation or other chemical complexities may alter effective surface energy and thereby change premelting behavior.
Predicted melting-onset temperatures and progression depend on the accuracy of the simulation potential and on heating rate.
Surface compositional segregation may modify atomic-mobility energy barriers.
